findings.evidence: The original deployment path ran the issuer directly via railway.toml start command without any bootstrap. Railway volumes are not mounted during preDeploy, so a one-off bootstrap job could not access /data. The startup seam (railway_issuer_startup.py) bridges this gap by idempotently bootstrapping at runtime after the volume is mounted but before the issuer starts.

The signing key (HUNTER_SOURCE_HANDLING_SIGNING_KEY) was previously required to be manually removed from the Railway Service after bootstrap. The startup seam now consumes the key for bootstrap and scrubs it from the process environment before exec'ing the issuer, so the signing key can remain as a Railway Secret without reaching the issuer process.

No parallel bootstrap, no parallel issuer, no duplicate authority model. The startup seam delegates entirely to the existing canonical bootstrap_source_handling_authority and exec's the existing canonical hunter_issue_agent_issuer.py with the same provenance resolver.

DFF-019 is added to docs/DEFECT_REGISTRY.json with scope scripts/ and railway.toml, and 18 regression test references. The preflight guard recomputes applicable families from changed paths, so any future deployment path that bypasses the startup seam is review-blocked.
